#171. Volvo's big batteries: We drive its updated 2028 plug-in hybrids

There’s just one thing we still don’t know: How much will they cost?

COPENHAGEN, Denmark—If we lived in the world that Volvo’s product planners expected back when the current XC90 debuted in 2015, both it and the smaller but related XC60 (which arrived in 2017) might have been the last of their kind as everything went electric. As we know, the future hasn’t turned out quite like that, especially in the critically important US market. At the same time, Europe and China are electrifying, which seems like an argument against spending resources on developing all-new replacements for models that might not have an eight-year lifespan in most markets.

So instead, Volvo has given the XC60 and XC90 another lifecycle refresh. The exterior styling tweaks are minimal; the bigger three-row XC90 had already been given a new look last year, and the XC60 now gains a similar grille and the same matrix headlights, for instance. And that’s no bad thing—both were, and remain, handsome shapes that are popular with Volvo’s customer base.

Instead, the Swedish automaker’s attention has been on bringing the technology up to date for model year 2028 standards. Which means a much bigger battery for the PHEVs, with sufficient capacity for a couple of days of daily driving for most of us before needing to be recharged. There’s also new, modern infotainment and interiors that are now even nicer to spend time in than before.

We first saw the revamped 2028 XC60 (and learned about its technical details and those of the XC90) in September, but with the cars going into production now and due to reach the first US customers in the first quarter of next year, we got the opportunity to spend some seat time with the updated cars.

Both the midsize XC60 and three-row XC90 use the same PHEV powertrain. Under the hood, there’s a 2.0 L four-cylinder direct-injection gasoline engine that generates 247 hp (184 kW) and 226 lb-ft (306 Nm) together with a 70 hp (50 kW), 122 ft-lb (165 Nm) electric motor, both of which drive the front wheels. At the rear axle there’s a second electric motor, with an output of 174 hp (130 kW) and 228 lb-ft (309 Nm). Combined output for the hybrid system is 455 hp (339 kW) and 560 lb-ft (759 Nm).

There’s also a much bigger battery, with a net capacity of 37.9 kWh (41.2 kWh gross). If you set the car’s mode to Pure, which relies solely on the rear electric motor for propulsion, that translates to an EPA range estimate of 78 miles (126 km) for the XC60 and 73 miles (116 km) for the larger, draggier XC90. Which is significant—when the average driver drives fewer than 30 miles a day, it means these PHEVs carry enough electrons for a couple of days of tailpipe-emissions-free driving before it needs to be plugged in again or the engine to fire up.

When it is time to plug it back in, expect it to take about four hours with a level 2 charger of at least 16 A, or 27 hours if you’re limited to 120 V. In Hybrid mode, where you get the benefit of both electric motors and the gas engine, Volvo expects a combined efficiency of 67 mpge in the XC60, and 61 mpge for the XC90.

Even if the gas engine is running and you’re in Hybrid or Power mode (which keeps the engine on all the time), you can drive these Volvos as if they were EVs with one-pedal driving: just move the transmission from D to B. The Volvos are always using their electric motors to slow the car before the friction brakes intervene, and in B you get the same amount of lift-off regen regardless of mode. For city traffic, it’s very effective. (In Pure, although only the rear motor deploys energy, both front and rear motors regen brake.)

In power mode, with all 455 hp unleashed, you can chirp the wheels on a wet day, but these model year 2028 cars are about one large male human heavier than the outgoing model year, both of which were already pretty heavy. So don’t expect performance-car performance. The XC60 is the sweeter to drive on a winding road, but both are entirely at home cruising on a highway or creeping along in a city, which is where cars like these spend the vast majority of their time. There’s more road intrusion into the cabin of the XC60—the larger Volvo rides on air suspension that does a much better job of filtering that out.

A first-drive event like this isn’t the best place to get a good read on real-world efficiency. We usually have to share cars with other journalists, and there’s limited time to drive on roads that may not be representative—too sinuous, or not enough traffic, for example. We need to try all the different drive modes and see how cars respond to different inputs. And it’s rare you’ll spend the entire day with one car, finishing at the same point you started.

That said, I can’t give you a definite read on range and efficiency for these two plug-ins. But my unscientific estimate is that my drive partner and I, in an XC60, drove about 60 km in a mix of city driving and higher speeds on the way to Malmo in Sweden, which is on the other side of a gigantic bridge, and we used about half the battery pack to do so. (Volvo asked us to put the PHEVs in Hold or Charge mode at 50 percent to leave some state of charge for whoever drove the cars after lunch.)

Thus, there was little charge left in the XC90 when it was my turn to drive the final stint back into Copenhagen. Since I wasn’t worried about combined efficiency, I ran the car in Charge mode for about 20 min, regenerating the battery from an indicated 10 km to an indicated 21 km, then switched to Pure once we reached the city, with about 16 km to go.

Volvo already had a reputation for great automotive interiors, and with this refresh, it has pushed things forward a little. There’s a new wood finish, new textiles, and new backlighting. The resemblance between the two interiors from the front seat is now quite strong, particularly since the test cars Volvo brought to Denmark wore identical color schemes inside.

Our final 1.6 km to the hotel took more than 30 minutes to negotiate thanks to a reception for very important people that apparently took place next to the hotel. Most of this jam was on one street, with our destination in sight, but the frustration was in part ameliorated by Volvo’s secret weapon: its seat massage function.

Lots of other OEMs offer massaging front seats, which inflate and deflate the internal air bladder to massage your shoulders, back, and sometimes butt. But none massage you with quite the firmness of a Volvo seat. And they have the power to distract you from terrible in-car situations, as I discovered when stuck in a V90 Cross Country with Nigel the Cat, whose way of remonstrating with me about his trip to the feline ophthalmologist was to scream at high volume until he ran out of breath, at which point he’d pant for a few minutes, then start again. The seat in that car is the only reason we both made it home safely. And so, in Copenhagen, I set the seat to pulse and did some box breathing.

As well as new interior materials, you’ll also notice a new infotainment screen in both cars. Gone are the old 9-inch displays, replaced by a new 11.2-inch touchscreen that stands a little proud of the dash rather than recessed into it. Just this one upgrade alone really lifts both interiors; the old, small screen was showing its age. Most Ars readers will recoil at the news that Gemini has replaced the previous Google Assistant, but at least the voice-recognition capabilities are improved. Gemini will still struggle with some commands—I asked it to tell me my current efficiency, which it failed at, but it’s rather good at looking stuff up on the Internet while I drive.

There are also some updated advanced driver-assistance systems, like a warning if cyclists approach your opening door, and an updated 360-degree parking view. But there’s no point-to-point assist like Mercedes is introducing, or a hands-free “level 2+” system like Super Cruise; Volvo’s experience with the EX90 may have left it a little gun-shy.

With a battery big enough for daily driving and a more modern interior experience, there’s a lot to like about both the 2029 XC60 and XC90. However, we still don’t know how much they’ll cost when they go on sale in Q1 next year. With twice the battery capacity, it’s reasonable to expect a slight price rise, but without knowing how much, it’s hard to say whether it’s a good deal or not.

What can you get for $30 these days? When it comes to tech, you might be surprised. Even as gadgets get more expensive, $30 can still go a long way, especially on Black Friday. For just $8, for instance, TP-Link’s Tapo smart plug will let you control the Christmas tree lights from your phone. You can also grab a decent pair of ANC-equipped earbuds for under $20, or spend even less on a clever set of rechargeable AA batteries. And it’s not just gadgets that are on sale: you can even sign up for a year of Disney Plus and Hulu for $4.99 ($8 off) a month.

Below, we’ve rounded up the best Black Friday deals for $30 or less, from charging accessories and smart home tech to earbuds, streaming subscriptions, games, and more. Whether you’re looking for practical stocking stuffers or want to treat yourself without spending too much, these are the deals that won’t put a (huge) dent in your wallet.

Apple’s latest AirTags feature an upgraded ultra-wideband chip for more precise location tracking, a noticeably louder speaker, and an expanded Bluetooth range. Read our review.

You can get an ad-supported Disney Plus and Hulu bundle for $4.99 a month ($8 off) for an entire year. Both streaming services feature a deep catalog of new and classic TV shows and movies, including The Simpsons, Andor, Toy Story 5, and The Fantastic Four: First Steps.

Do you ever wish you could turn on your coffee maker or hit the light switch without getting up? The SwitchBot Bot lets you do that. All you need to do is stick the inexpensive contraption on a standard button or rocker switch, which will allow you to control or schedule your pet feeder, garage door, and a wide range of other devices from your smartphone.

Who needs magnets when you have suction cups? Octobuddy’s cheap silicone mount works with most phones to provide hands-free flexibility whenever necessary. It features 24 single-sided cups, which allow you to stick your phone to a mirror, window, or any other surface you think will provide that perfect TikTok angle.

The Chamera is not a good camera, but that’s not the point. Kodak’s charming, keychain-friendly tchotchke lets you snap lo-fi memories on a whim, with an ultra-small 1.6-megapixel sensor, a built-in LED flash, and the tiniest amount of storage.

Hoto’s rechargeable screwdriver is ideal for small repairs. It offers three torque modes, a rotational speed of up to 220RPM, and a helpful circular LED to illuminate dark spaces. The durable case also holds all 25 steel bits and an extension bar for getting into hard-to-reach places.

Rechargeable AA batteries are handy until it’s time to charge them. Most wall chargers let you refill four, maybe six, at once. Zepath’s clever solution is to ship them in an easy-to-use USB-C charging case that charges eight simultaneously. The batteries themselves are long-lasting, too.

An HBO Max Basic subscription provides access to shows like A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, The Last of Us, and The Pitt, as well as films like Superman and Weapons. You can get a year of the monthly ad-supported subscription for $5.49 a month (about $6 off) until December 1st.

The Wuben G5 flashlight is as small as a Zippo lighter, yet far more versatile, with a bright, rotatable light that can shine in numerous colors. It features USB-C charging and has an adjustable clip.

The original LifeStraw was designed for those heading into the backcountry. The new LifeStraw Sip? Not so much. The reusable steel straw is geared more toward travelers than outdoor enthusiasts, though fortunately it still manages to remove about 99.99 percent of microplastics, bacteria, and parasites from your drinking water.

Peacock is a great way to catch up on a wealth of content from NBC’s various networks, whether you plan to rewatch The Office or catch up on all things Bravo. A Premium subscription also grants access to films from studios like Universal Pictures and Dreamworks, along with live sports and a host of Peacock Originals.

Anker’s 621 Magnetic Battery is a slim, 5,000mAh charger that can attach magnetically to the back of any MagSafe-ready iPhone.

TP-Link’s Wi-Fi smart plug lets you remotely control lamps, fans, and other appliances using your phone or voice commands. It supports Matter, so it works with all major smart home platforms to set schedules and timers to automatically turn devices on or off.

Paramount Plus Premium provides access to live sports as well as movies and shows from both platforms, including Tales of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, a host of Yellowstone spinoffs, Star Trek shows, Sonic the Hedgehog 3, Twin Peaks, Dexter, and more.

Amazon’s last-gen Fire TV Stick 4K Plus streams in 4K and supports Dolby Atmos, Dolby Vision, and Alexa Plus. It also ships with the redesigned Fire OS and, unlike more recent models, still lets you sideload Android TV apps.

With 12.4mm drivers, active noise cancellation, and an IP54 rating, the CMF Buds 2A offer high-end features at an affordable price. You can also customize the sound, adjust ANC levels, and find the earbuds using the Nothing X app.

Twelve South’s entry-level Bluetooth transmitter delivers up to 25 hours of continuous use and lets you connect up to two pairs of headphones to an in-flight entertainment system, making it a great travel companion no matter where you’re going.

In Catan, up to four players strategically compete and trade for resources. The iconic board game ends when one player reaches 10 “victory points,” which is achieved by constructing a sprawling civilization of roads, settlements, and cities using sheep, ore, wheat, and wood.

Azul is a game in which you arrange patterned tiles in order to create the most beautiful tapestry possible. Arranging tiles in a strategic sequence will help you build your score while limiting your opponents’ ability to grow theirs.

Halo: Campaign Evolved lets you revisit the original Halo: Combat Evolved campaign with better graphics, updated controls, and improved sound. The well-crafted remake also adds three new missions starring Master Chief and Sgt. Johnson, which take place before the main campaign. Read our review.

No one should have to deal with a rat’s nest behind their desk when devices like Anker’s 2-in-1 USB-C cable exist. The handy USB-C cable splits at the end, giving you the ability to charge up to two devices from a single port. That means you can split power between a phone and tablet or juice a 16-inch MacBook Pro to 50 percent in just 20 minutes using a single port.

The Witcher 3 lets you explore the war-torn Northern Kingdoms as Geralt of Rivia while preparing to face the mysterious Wild Hunt. The recent remaster adds improved visuals, smoother combat, and better movement, cementing the game’s status as one of the best RPGs of all time.

Iniu’s P55-E2 Power Bank is an ultra-slim three-port USB charger that’s capable of fully recharging an iPhone 16 twice. It supports charging speeds of up to 45W via a USB-C port, which can deliver fast recharging for a range of gadgets.

Glocusent’s clip-in reading light features five brightness levels and multiple color temperature settings, ranging from a soft, warm glow that’s great for late-night reading to a brighter light that’s perfect for daytime use. The slim USB light easily slips into your pocket, too, so you can read anywhere, from a cozy bed to a dimly lit train.

LIFX’s dimmable, color-changing bulbs offer Wi-Fi connectivity, simple setup, and Matter compatibility, so they work with any major smart home platform. The company is currently trialing a Thread beta that will bring the option to add Thread connectivity to all its Matter devices.

The ChomChom is a reusable roller that works great for removing unwanted pet hair from furniture, allowing you to skip lint rollers, vacuuming, and other cleaning tools in a pinch.

Apple TV offers ad-free streaming of original shows and movies, including shows like Severance, Silo, Slow Horses, and Pluribus. The service also features a rotating selection of films, along with live Formula 1 races and Major League Soccer matches.

Anker’s Qi2 charging pads support wireless charging speeds of up to 15W, and their 5-foot cable shouldn’t feel constricting if you need to move the charger around.

Blink’s Mini 2K Plus is a small plug-in security camera that lets you monitor your home or pets with 2K video, motion detection, and color night vision. It also offers two-way audio, a built-in siren, and Alexa support; however, some features, including person and vehicle detection, require a Blink subscription.

Attending a live concert? You can protect your hearing with Loop’s Quiet 2 earplugs. They pack up to 24dB (SNR) of noise reduction and come with four eartip sizes, allowing them to accommodate a range of ear shapes.

Crunchyroll is an anime-centric streaming service that offers ad-free access to shows like One Piece, Jujutsu Kaisen, The Apothecary Diaries, and Black Clover, with new episodes available shortly after they air in Japan.

Logitech’s Pop is a cute, simple wireless mouse with an ambidextrous design and the ability to switch between up to three devices. It supports customization through the Logi Options Plus app and can last for several months on a single charge.

Logitech’s G502 Hero has most of the same features as one of our top choices among gaming mice, the G502 Lightspeed, except it’s wired. If you’re okay with that, this is an excellent mouse that you can usually find for $50 or less.

The proliferation of miniature screens continues with Ugreen’s latest Nexode USB-C Cable, which features a full-color LCD screen on one end that displays current power draw (up to 240W). It also supports 480Mbps data transfer speeds and, unlike similar power meter-equipped cables, lets you turn off the screen when needed.

The Tile Pro is the company’s loudest Bluetooth tracker, one that benefits from a 500-foot range. It also features a user-replaceable battery, unlike some other Tiles, and works with both iOS and Android devices.

Anker’s jack-of-all-trades travel adapter packs enough ports to refill your devices during some downtime. It features one AC outlet, two USB-C ports (one tops out at 20W), and two USB-A ports. It’s not the fastest wall charger, but it’s a solid choice when you can find it at a discount.

The Kobo Remote lets you turn pages on a compatible Kobo e-reader with the click of a button, so you can keep reading without reaching for the screen. It connects directly over Bluetooth and features a curved, handheld design that doesn’t require clipping anything onto your e-reader.

The second-gen Ring Indoor Cam lets you keep an eye on your place in 1080p, with support for motion detection alerts, a live feed, and color night vision.

Workpro’s EDC is a lightweight folding utility knife with a side-mounted button that lets you flick it open and closed with one hand. It uses standard utility blades, which you can easily replace using a spring-loaded plate, making it handy for breaking down cardboard boxes and other tasks.

Lamicall’s cord organizers use magnetic clasps to keep cables in place, preventing them from slipping behind desks, shelves, and other furniture when unplugged.

Nalgene’s lightweight, 16-ounce water bottle features a narrow opening for sipping, a leakproof lid, and a slim design that fits in cup holders. It’s made from durable, BPA- and BPS-free plastic, with measurement markings along the side and dishwasher-safe construction.

This tiny cordless driver comes with five double-ended bits for most basic around-the-house projects and Ikea-level builds.

During Black Friday, the Anker 100W Universal Charger is on sale for $59.99 at Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart, a $20 discount from its list price. That’s a few dollars lower than the previous best, with both the dark gray and silver versions available from all three retailers. With four USB ports and support for over 200 countries, you can keep all of your devices charged wherever you end up.

Anker’s durable travel adapter delivers up to 100W of power and works in over 200 countries. It doesn’t support AC plugs, but it does offer a trio of USB-C ports and a nifty LCD display to keep tabs on the charge percentage.

Anker’s travel charger supports outlets in over 200 countries, including Type A for the United States, Canada, Japan, and China; Type C for the European Union; and Type G for the UK and Singapore. It doesn’t support Type I, the outlet used in Australia, New Zealand, and Argentina. Also, there’s no AC adapter. It’s a USB-only affair. To that end, you can charge up to four devices at once, with three USB-C ports and one USB-A port, with two of the USB-C ports capable of delivering up to 100W when used individually. There’s even a tiny display on the unit that lets you check how much power is going to your devices at a glance.

#166. Books, bikes, and The Burbs: These are Ars staff’s holiday gift picks for 2026

We polled the Ars staff about their favorite pickups this year; here’s the list.

The holiday shopping season is upon us, and as is our custom, we’re here with a list of Ars staffers’ favorite recent purchases that could make good gifts. (Or maybe they might be a gift you get yourself!)

Rather than try to write a definitive “best gifts for your sister or brother” type of guide, we simply polled Ars staffers on stuff they’ve actually bought this year that they recommend. The thinking is that if we’re into it, hopefully some of you or your friends or family might be. As such, there’s no rhyme or reason to these selections, really; it’s just a list of stuff we bought that we’re happy about. It’s heavy on interesting books and cycling accessories, but there are some gadgets and the like in here, too.

For each gadget (or whatever else it might be), we have a brief description of how or why we’ve been using this particular thing and why we would recommend it. Our picks are ordered by price, from lowest to highest. Note, though, that the prices of these products are listed as they were when the list was written. Online retailers often adjust prices frequently, especially around Black Friday, so just a heads up: The price might be different by the time you read this.

Also, a callout to the Ars commentariat: If you have your own holiday buying recommendations, feel free to share them. We or some fellow readers might take your advice if you suggest something good! Happy holidays!

Dungeon Crawler Carl by Matt Dinniman – $13

I understand the convenience and space-savings that e-readers bring. My 2011 Kindle Touch goes with me everywhere I carry my travel backpack, but I’m still a softy for physical books when I’m sitting at home on a lazy Sunday. What started as something of a fanfic send-up of LitRPGs has quickly blossomed into a massive sensation of a series filled with far more depth, heart, and character than the initial premise might indicate. Author Matt Dinniman has an accessible style that will grip any reader with a taste for whimsical adventure. Just be warned that if you leave the books under the tree, you might not see much of the recipient until New Year’s.

Undersea War: The Battle to Control the Cables and Pipelines That Connect Our World by Elisabeth Braw– $30

Lightning Beneath the Sea: The Race to Wire the World and the Dawn of the Information Age by James M. Tabor– $32

Two excellent books that help describe how the Internet’s undersea backbone became a globe-spanning reality were published in 2026. Together, they form a great gift pairing for anyone interested in how humanity first achieved near-instantaneous communication across the world’s oceans—and how the first trans-Atlantic telegraph cable paved the way for a global network of subsea data cables that now faces growing risks from geopolitical conflicts.

James Tabor’s Lightning Beneath the Sea dives into the astounding real-life story of how American entrepreneur Cyrus Field, lacking in expertise but driven by personal fervor, set out to achieve peace on Earth by laying a 2,000-mile telegraph cable made of copper across the Atlantic seafloor in 1866.

To pull off the feat, Field managed to convince some of the greatest innovators and scientific luminaries of his day, such as Samuel F.B. Morse, Lord Kelvin, and Michael Faraday, to join his venture. He also refitted the SS Great Eastern steamship, the largest passenger liner ship built to date, as a cable-laying vessel.

That first ocean-spanning telegraph cable gave rise to more such cables for transmitting messages around the world. Eventually copper gave way to a network of subsea fiber-optic cables that became the Internet’s undersea backbone, and the modern world also became interlinked with submarine power cables and underwater pipelines for carrying oil and gas.

But all that undersea infrastructure is now facing growing danger from the threat of deliberate sabotage, as described in Elisabeth Braw’s book Undersea War. Her book provides a sobering but enlightening look at why subsea cables and pipelines are becoming more tempting targets amid rising geopolitical tensions and conflicts—and how governments and companies are responding to recent cable-cutting incidents around the world.

Read Ars Technica’s Q&A with Elisabeth Braw about Undersea War.

The Burbs Collector’s Edition 4K Blu-ray – $32

It’s a little-remembered film for most people, but I absolutely love The Burbs. Sure, it’s more Halloween fare than Christmas, but last year I picked The Thing, so clearly “1980s movies for October” is my December viewing MO.

Starring Tom Hanks, Carrie Fisher, and Corey Feldman, this is a dry, hilarious send-up of suburban life with a horror-adjacent mystery that keeps you guessing. (It’s not scary, though.) I hardly ever hear anyone else talk about this movie, but I love it, and it only recently came out in 4K, so I’m taking this opportunity to shout it out.

How Apollo Flew to the Moon by David Woods – $35

If you’re a technically minded Ars reader looking for a nice book to snuggle down with over the holidays, David Woods’ How Apollo Flew to the Moon could be just the thing. (There’s also an audiobook version.) Woods has an accessible style that breaks down complex engineering challenges and their solutions into easily digestible chunks that clarify without oversimplifying. He uses that style to take readers on a detailed trip through the machinery of Project Apollo, from the launch facilities and Mission Control all the way to the specific mechanics of how to navigate to and land on the Moon—and, from there, how to return safely to Earth.

Ever wondered about the insane engineering that let the Saturn V’s first stage burn almost 15 tons of fuel every second as it powered the crew into orbit? Or how to pinpoint a spacecraft’s centimeter-precise distance from Earth on its way to the Moon? Or how Apollo crews tracked their own position with stellar navigation, using sextants and star sightings? Or what a REFSMMAT is, or how television transmissions from the Moon worked, or how they got those crazy lunar buggies onto the Moon’s surface? All these questions and more are given beautifully complete and technically satisfying answers, suitable for both the curious layperson and also the interested engineer. Grab this book and stun your family at Christmas with amazing Apollo trivia—as a bonus, you’ll have the knowledge to make your “We never landed on the Moon!” conspiracy theorist uncle so angry that he stops talking and watches football in grumpy silence! Everyone wins!

As someone who grew up in the classic era of 16-bit SNES RPGs, this 40th anniversary tribute to the series’ history is everything I could have ever wanted in a modern entry. I haven’t properly played through a Final Fantasy entry since the days of Final Fantasy X on PlayStation 2, but when friends kept nudging me that this was the perfect “Nick game,” I figured I should probably take a look. There’s a free six-hour demo available on supported platforms if you’re still on the fence about picking this one up, but don’t be surprised if you end up grabbing a copy for yourself.

Govee Star Light Projector (Nebula Effect) – $70

For the past couple of years, I’ve been transforming my tiny office into a sanctuary in the evenings, since I do most of my writing (and gaming) in here then. It started with Govee Hexa panels, then came an RGB TV backlight, then colorful smart bulbs for the built-in light fixtures. I topped it off with the Star Light projector, which coats the ceiling in a soothing, ever-shifting, immersive stars-and-nebula effect.

It’s probably not for everybody, but my office is tiny, and I spend a lot of time here both for work and for fun. Tapping a button to completely shift the vibe is surprisingly effective at making it a room I don’t mind spending time in even after I’ve been working in it all day.

Easily my favorite impulse purchase of 2026, the FM-1 is a great gift for curious tinkerers and experienced musicians alike. At around $70 or less, you don’t have to break the bank to get fiddling. A perfectly decent stock synthesizer on its own, the real fun starts when you begin experimenting with the community firmware packages that transform the synth into anything from a multi-track groovebox to one of the more hilarious ways that I’ve ever tried to play Doom.

Trek BellBeats digital bike bell and speaker – $125One of the great things about cycling is the chance to be alone with my thoughts—just me and my bike. But that can be too much of a good thing on longer zone 2 rides and centuries. Sporting the size and shape of an old-school bicycle bell, the Trek BellBeats is a safer alternative to donning headphones while on the bike.BellBeats pair with your phone via Bluetooth and will play music at a volume loud enough to enjoy your tunes or hear navigation prompts, but they are not so loud that the music drowns out traffic (or the radar on your bike computer). They can be mounted on just about any non-aero handlebars, charge over USB-C, and offer up to six hours of playtime. And as a bonus, they double as a bicycle bell.

I use Bluetooth headphones most of the time, but frustratingly, they don’t work with voice chat on the PlayStation 5, and I needed a good-quality headset for my Friday night multiplayer gaming sessions.

I’ve always liked Fractal Design’s PC cases, so I decided to roll the dice on their affordable-for-the-quality, over-ear headphones. They support Bluetooth, but they also have a USB dongle, so they can be used for voice chat on game consoles, too.

I was surprised by how much I like them, and despite buying them just for the PS5, I’ve ended up using them in other contexts. Part of that is because they’re very comfortable, and the design avoids my glasses frames well.

I also like that, although they are gaming headphones with all the expected bells and whistles for that, they don’t have an over-the-top design.

If you’re in the market for mid-range wireless gaming headphones that look like something you could actually wear in public without embarrassment, these fit the bill so far.

Povec C1 Performance Sunglasses – $250Photochromic sunglasses are incredibly useful for outdoor workouts. Two of the most popular bike trails near me run through forest preserves, and the lighting changes steadily as the forest canopy closes in or spreads out. My default sunglasses are a cheap, $28 pair from Rockbros.Unlike other photochromic glasses, which change tints via a pokey chemical reaction, the Povec C1 uses a battery to switch between tints in a second. All the rider (or runner) needs to do is swipe the right temple and the lenses will darken or lighten almost instantaneously. The C1 charges via a small USB-C port, and the Povec claims 28 days of battery life with four hours of daily usage. I’ve used them off and on for about six weeks and have only had to charge them once.

The C1 comes in three frame colors and either Green Revo or Gold Revo glasses and is an excellent stocking stuffer for the runner, cyclist, or skier in your life.

Garmin Varia RCT715 radar camera tail light – $300Last spring, a friend of mine was the victim of a hit-and-run while on a ride. Although she wasn’t seriously hurt, her brand-new bike was totaled. The driver got an unwelcome surprise a couple of days later when the police knocked on his front door and arrested him. My friend was riding with a Garmin Varia RCT715, a combination taillight and radar with a camera. The 1080p/30 fps camera captured the car’s license plate, making it possible for the police to identify the driver.More than 90 percent of my riding is on roads, and I don’t feel fully comfortable without my Varia. I have it paired with my Garmin Edge 1050 bike computer, but it will work with most other brands via ANT+. The Varia detects approaching vehicles at 140 meters, and I have it set to record video starting when a car is detected and for 30 seconds after it passes. Battery life is up to six hours, depending on whether the taillight is solid or flashing, and video is saved on a 16GB microSD memory card.

My YouTube algorithm has recently fed me videos of testers using an angle grinder to cut through decent bike locks in under a minute. I’ve never seen an angle grinder-assisted theft in person, but I’ve seen enough heaps of bike parts around town to know people’s rides are getting jacked somewhere. As someone known to be neurotic about leaving my bike outside my purview, I’m looking for added security measures to ease my stress.Enter the Hiplok, which, according to the tests I’ve watched, will turn multiple angle-grinder blades to dust. Do bike thieves carry several discs, and will they spend about 15 minutes trying to break this lock? I don’t know, but I have my doubts. At nearly $400, it’s about as expensive as it gets to secure your ride, but when your bike tops $5,000, it’s probably worth the added theft deterrence and peace of mind.

Santa left this one last year, and the rest of my handheld collection has felt neglected since. Sporting a Snapdragon 8 Elite (now dubbed the Dragonwing Q8) chip, excellent ergonomics, and a 6-inch 120Hz AMOLED screen, it’s the perfect balance between size and horsepower. The Android unit is capable enough to play most anything you can throw at it, without the bulk of a Steam Deck or the bloat of a Windows handheld. Thanks to things like Proton, FEX translation, and software like DroidDeck or GameNative, there isn’t much I can’t use it for. Streaming consoles or PC gaming? Check. Access to Steam, GOG, Epic, Rockstar libraries? Check. High-end native Android gaming? Yup. Emulate anything under the sun? You’re covered there, too. The latest Odin 3 Portal hardware revision gets a larger 7-inch screen and a base RAM configuration of 12GB over the original model’s 8GB. I may have to ask Mr. Claus about an upgrade…

#164. Finland's Prime Minister Sanna Marin concedes election

Finland’s left-wing Prime Minister Sanna Marin conceded defeat on Sunday in the Nordic country’s parliamentary election as the opposition right-wing National Coalition Party (NCP) claimed victory in a tightly fought contest.

The pro-business NCP was expected to win 48 of the 200 seats in parliament, narrowly ahead of the nationalist Finns Party with 46 seats and Marin’s Social Democrats on 43 seats, justice ministry election data showed with all ballots counted.

“We got the biggest mandate,” NCP leader Petteri Orpo said in a speech to followers, vowing to “fix Finland” and its economy.

He will get the first chance at forming a coalition to obtain majority in parliament as Marin’s era as prime minister was expected to end.

Popular abroad, at home Marin faces battle to keep her job

“We have gained support, we have gained more seats (in parliament). That’s an excellent achievement, even if we did not finish first today,” the prime minister said in a speech to party members.

Marin, 37, the world’s youngest prime minister when she took office in 2019, is considered by fans around the globe as a millennial role model for progressive new leaders, but at home she has faced criticism for her partying and her government’s public spending.

Finnish Prime Minister Sanna Marin takes drug test following partying backlash

While she remains very popular among many Finns, particularly young moderates, she antagonized some conservatives with lavish spending on pensions and education they see as not frugal enough.

The NCP has led in polls for almost two years although its lead had melted away in recent months. It has promised to curb spending and stop the rise of public debt, which has reached just over 70% of GDP since Marin took office in 2019.

Orpo accused Marin of eroding Finland’s economic resilience at a time when Europe’s energy crisis, driven by Russia’s war in Ukraine, has hit the country hard and the cost of living has increased.

Orpo has said he will negotiate with all groups to obtain a majority in parliament, while Marin has said her Social Democrats may govern with the NCP but will not go into government with the Finns Party.

Marin called the Finns Party “openly racist” during a debate in January – an accusation the nationalist group rejected.

The Finns Party’s main goal is to reduce what leader Riikka Purra has called “harmful” immigration from developing countries outside the European Union. It also calls for austerity policies to curb deficit spending, a stance it shares with the NCP.

Most notable of Marin’s foreign policy actions has been her push, along with President Sauli Niinisto, for the country to make a watershed policy U-turn by seeking NATO membership in the wake of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

That process is now almost complete, with Helsinki expected to join within days after all the Western defense alliance’s 30 members approved the accession.

#162. In Iran, child marriage risks complicated by war

War, poverty and disrupted schooling could put more girls in Iran at risk of child marriage, rights advocates have warned.

For a girl still at school, marriage can mean leaving her education behind, becoming pregnant before adulthood and growing dependent on her family and husband.

In Iran, rights advocates warn that war and mounting financial hardship could expose more girls to those risks.

The warning comes as the first International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage is observed on November 27. The day was established during the UN General Assembly in 2025.

Although there is no evidence linking child marriages to the war, cases illustrate the danger faced by girls married as children, often with limited means of escaping abuse. Gaps in Iran's marriage statistics also make it difficult to measure the impact of the conflict.

In one case cited by the Iranian human rights news agency HRANA, a 14-year-old girl in Kerman province who had recently given birth was reportedly killed by her husband. Skylar Thompson, deputy director of Human Rights Activists in Iran, said the girl had reportedly been forced to marry at 13.

"While these cases cannot be directly attributed to the war, there are substantial grounds for concern that deteriorating socioeconomic conditions are placing more girls at risk," Thompson told DW.

Iran Open Data's analysis of the Civil Registration Organization's statistical yearbook identified 14,039 registered marriages involving girls under 15 between roughly March 2025 and March 2026. They accounted for just over 3% of all registered marriages.

The figure excludes girls aged 15 to 17. UNICEF defines child marriage as a formal marriage or informal union involving someone under 18.

Thompson said 31,646 marriages involving girls under 15 were registered in 2020–2021, indicating a longer-term decline in recorded cases.

But the latest figures largely predate the war, which began on February 28, 2026.

"The absence of recent, disaggregated statistics, coupled with the prevalence of unregistered marriages, makes it difficult to determine whether child marriage has increased since the outbreak of the war," she said.

The conflict has intensified pressures that can contribute to child marriage: lost income, difficulty staying in school and girls' financial dependence on their families.

In its October assessment, the World Bank described damage to infrastructure, disrupted trade and declining purchasing power, forecasting a 7.7% economic contraction in 2026/27.

Thompson said that families facing severe hardship may see marriage as a way to reduce household expenses, transfer financial responsibility or secure their daughters' future. Government-backed marriage loans can also create financial incentives for some disadvantaged families to arrange marriages involving minors, she added.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Hossein Raeesi, a lawyer and adjunct professor in Carleton University's Department of Law and Legal Studies in Ottawa, Canada, described a similar risk.

When families cannot meet a girl's living costs and education or other prospects are unavailable, they may push her toward marriage or force her into it, he told DW, while acknowledging that statistics on changes in numbers of child marriages since the war are still unavailable.

Displacement can further weaken children's access to education and protection. On March 12, the UN refugee agency estimated that up to 3.2 million people had been temporarily displaced within Iran, based on preliminary assessments. That was an early-war estimate, rather than a current displacement figure.

Thompson said displacement and disrupted schooling could isolate girls from teachers, social workers and others who might recognize pressure to marry and intervene on their behalf.

Financial dependence, limited independent legal assistance and insufficient shelters can leave girls with few alternatives, particularly when those arranging a marriage are also their legal guardians.

Article 1041 of Iran's Civil Code allows girls under 13 and boys under 15 to marry with guardian consent and court approval. Iranian law therefore provides no blanket prohibition on marriage below the age of 18.

"Although Iranian law formally recognizes consent as a condition of marriage, it provides inadequate practical safeguards against familial coercion," Thompson told DW.

Raeesi said preventing a marriage was insufficient if a girl remained under pressure at home. Leaving home could also expose her to further danger without safe accommodation and practical support.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The concerns also extend to the online space. An investigation published by Human Rights Activists in Iran in October reported that the government-licensed matchmaking platform Adam and Eve displayed girls aged 13 to 17 as prospective spouses. Those findings do not establish how many marriages resulted, or whether the war increased them.

Raeesi called for a minimum marriage age of 18 for both sexes, alongside preventive intervention, financial assistance, education and safe accommodation.

"Education alone is not enough," he said. Families also need the means to support their children.

Thompson urged targeted financial assistance, measures to keep girls in school, confidential reporting channels and independent legal support. Safe accommodation must be accessible without permission from guardians who may themselves be responsible for coercion, she said.

According to rights advocates, effective protection means that a girl under pressure to marry can say no without losing her home, her safety or her chance to continue school.

#161. The absolute best Black Friday deals we’ve found (so far)

This year’s Black Friday deals have launched in waves over the past several weeks, but now the floodgates have officially opened. You can now take advantage of the lowest prices we’ve seen in-store and online for video games, wireless earbuds, TVs, e-readers, robot vacuums, and so much more. We can’t guarantee a deal you’ve had your eye on will last through Cyber Monday; however, if prior years are any indication, most will stick around through the long holiday weekend.

As usual, we sorted through thousands of deals to find the ones truly worth sharing, with an eye for the products and services we’ve tested here at The Verge. With prices up across multiple categories due to RAMageddon, some deals may not seem as big as in prior years. For example, Apple’s latest MacBook Air recently fell to its pre-price-hike level for the first time since July. That’s a deal to us, and several other discounts are taking a similar shape. We’ll provide context when possible and keep this post updated throughout the day.

Apple’s AirPods Pro 3 deliver the best noise cancellation and sound quality of any AirPods yet, along with a more comfortable, secure fit and improved water resistance. They also feature built-in heart rate tracking for workouts and support live translations for a handful of languages. Read our review.

You can get an ad-supported Disney Plus and Hulu bundle for $4.99 a month ($8 off) for an entire year. Both streaming services feature a deep catalog of new and classic TV shows and movies, including The Simpsons, Andor, Toy Story 5, and The Fantastic Four: First Steps.

Anker’s durable travel adapter delivers up to 100W of power and works in over 200 countries. It doesn’t support AC plugs, but it does offer a trio of USB-C ports and a nifty LCD display to keep tabs on the charge percentage.

With a 4.3-inch E Ink screen, the Xteink X4 is smaller and more pocketable than any Kindle and Kobo model currently available. It has some drawbacks — it’s limited to TXT and EPUB files — but it’s great for tinkering; it also has a magnetic mount so you can stick it to the back of MagSafe-ready phones.

The Nintendo Switch 2 features a 7.9-inch LCD display, magnetically attached Joy-Con 2 controllers, backward compatibility with most original Switch games, and exclusive titles like Donkey Kong Bananza and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Read our review.

An HBO Max Basic subscription provides access to shows like A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, The Last of Us, and The Pitt, as well as films like Superman and Weapons. You can get a year of the monthly ad-supported subscription for $5.49 a month (about $6 off) until December 1st.

The Eufy Omni C28 combines excellent mopping performance with a small self-cleaning dock that’s well suited for apartments and other smaller spaces. It navigates around furniture and into tight areas with ease, while its roller mop does a great job cleaning hard floors.

Do you ever wish you could turn on your coffee maker or hit the light switch without getting up? The SwitchBot Bot lets you do that. All you need to do is stick the inexpensive contraption on a standard button or rocker switch, which will allow you to control or schedule your pet feeder, garage door, and a wide range of other devices from your smartphone.

Apple’s latest AirTags feature an upgraded ultra-wideband chip for more precise location tracking, a noticeably louder speaker, and an expanded Bluetooth range. Read our review.

The Chamera is not a good camera, but that’s not the point. Kodak’s charming, keychain-friendly tchotchke lets you snap lo-fi memories on a whim, with an ultra-small 1.6-megapixel sensor, a built-in LED flash, and the tiniest amount of storage.

LIFX’s dimmable, color-changing bulbs offer Wi-Fi connectivity, simple setup, and Matter compatibility, so they work with any major smart home platform. The company is currently trialing a Thread beta that will bring the option to add Thread connectivity to all its Matter devices.

Apple’s latest MacBook Air features an M5 chip and starts with 512GB of storage, with significantly faster performance than prior generations. It’s still an excellent machine despite the higher base price, especially given the battery life and speakers. Read our review.

Who needs magnets when you have suction cups? Octobuddy’s cheap silicone mount works with most phones to provide hands-free flexibility whenever necessary. It features 24 single-sided cups, which allow you to stick your phone to a mirror, window, or any other surface you think will provide that perfect TikTok angle.

Peacock is a great way to catch up on a wealth of content from NBC’s various networks, whether you plan to rewatch The Office or catch up on all things Bravo. A Premium subscription also grants access to films from studios like Universal Pictures and Dreamworks, along with live sports and a host of Peacock Originals.

The P9 is great if you need more storage for your Nintendo Switch 2. The microSD Express card offers sequential read speeds of up to 800MB/s, but only gadgets with a microSD Express card slot can take full advantage of the highest speeds. That includes certain cameras, tablets, and drones with a microSD USH-I slot.

The Fanttik X9 Pro can inflate a car tire in under a minute, making routine maintenance fast and easy. There are four one-click presets for cars, motorcycles, bikes, and balls, along with a manual mode that reaches a maximum pressure of 150 PSI.

Apple’s 11th-gen iPad is the successor to the previous 10-gen model. It has a new A16 chip and few other changes — and is the only Apple tablet to not support Apple Intelligence.

No one should have to deal with a rat’s nest behind their desk when devices like Anker’s 2-in-1 USB-C cable exist. The handy USB-C cable splits at the end, giving you the ability to charge up to two devices from a single port. That means you can split power between a phone and tablet or juice a 16-inch MacBook Pro to 50 percent in just 20 minutes using a single port.

The Wuben G5 flashlight is as small as a Zippo lighter, yet far more versatile, with a bright, rotatable light that can shine in numerous colors. It features USB-C charging and has an adjustable clip.

Sony’s XM4 noise-canceling headphones were so good, the company brought them back with a few minor improvements. They still offer great ANC, a timeless foldable design, and delivering performance nearly on par with Sony’s newer flagships at a fraction of the cost.

Govee’s Table Lamp 2 is way more fun than your average table lamp. The color-changing device boasts built-in scheduling and more than 60 dynamic lighting effects, including preset scenes for various holidays. You can even create custom color combos for when “Dandelion” and other presets just aren’t cutting it.

Compared to the last-gen base Kindle model (currently $119.99), the Paperwhite is a much better value. It features waterproofing, better battery life, faster page-turning speeds, and a higher pixel density screen that’s slightly larger (7 inches vs. 6 inches)

The water-resistant Sonos Play sits between the Roam 2 and Move 2, offering a balance of portability and room-filling sound. It delivers up to 24 hours of battery life, with a built-in loop for easy carrying. You can also use it as a power bank and pair it with other Sonos speakers over Bluetooth when Wi-Fi isn’t available. Read our review.

Rechargeable AA batteries are handy until it’s time to charge them. Most wall chargers let you refill four, maybe six, at once. Zepath’s clever solution is to ship them in an easy-to-use USB-C charging case that charges eight simultaneously. The batteries themselves are long-lasting, too.

The Ring 5 is a fantastic entry point for new users. While short on improvements over its thicker predecessor, it’s hard not to appreciate that it manages to deliver similar battery life despite being thinner. Read our review.

007 First Light, a third-person stealth action game from the studio behind Hitman, is arguably the best action game we’ve played this year. It features a wide variety of missions that have you sneaking through enemy territory, engaging in hand-to-hand combat, and taking part in high-speed car chases — you know, classic Bond stuff. Read our review.

Amazon’s last-gen Fire TV Stick 4K Plus streams in 4K and supports Dolby Atmos, Dolby Vision, and Alexa Plus. It also ships with the redesigned Fire OS and, unlike more recent models, still lets you sideload Android TV apps.

The Apple Watch Series 12 introduces AI-powered Audio Intelligence features, including sound recognition alerts, Live Rewind, and Siri Recap. It can also track your heart rate every five seconds, even when you’re not exercising, and offers faster charging than prior models. Read our review.

Fanttik’s rechargeable electric screwdriver features three adjustable torque settings, a built-in LED light, and 16 S2 hardened steel bits for tackling everything from furniture assembly to small electronics repairs. It also comes with a magnetic storage case and supports USB-C.

Anker’s 25,000mAh power bank sports two built-in USB-C cables (one of which is retractable), plus one USB-C and USB-A port. It tops out at 165W when charging two devices simultaneously, or 130W when charging three or four.

The cost continues to fall on Samsung’s latest, best foldable yet. The Z Fold 8 is a passport-style phone, like the iPhone Duo, with fast performance and slick design.

You likely won’t find wireless earbuds with a more striking appearance than Nothing’s Ear 3A. They also sound fantastic, boast active noise cancellation, and offer robust EQ settings, making them a great pick for the price. Read our review.

Acer’s answer to the MacBook Neo, with an Intel Core 5 processor, 8GB of RAM, 120Hz display, and speedy Thunderbolt 4 ports. We’re still testing this one, but it’s showing promise for an affordable choice.

Outside of the Integrity, few spacecraft made as big a splash in 2026 as the one Ryland Grace piloted in Project Hail Mary. And now, thanks to Lego, you can construct a microscale replica of the titular Hail Mary, complete with a miniature Rocky figure.

Hoto’s rechargeable screwdriver is ideal for small repairs. It offers three torque modes, a rotational speed of up to 220RPM, and a helpful circular LED to illuminate dark spaces. The durable case also holds all 25 steel bits and an extension bar for getting into hard-to-reach places.

Sony’s DualSense Wireless Controller for the PlayStation 5 features immersive haptic feedback and resistance triggers, which feel great to use. It offers a built-in mic, a 3.5mm headphone jack, and a mute button; it also works with PC, macOS, and mobile devices via Bluetooth or USB-C.

Apple’s most affordable laptop uses the same A18 Pro chip found in the iPhone 16 Pro. It features a vibrant 13-inch display, surprisingly good speakers, and 8GB of RAM, making it a solid option for students and anyone who needs a laptop for everyday tasks. Read our review.

Ember’s latest smart mug is designed to keep your coffee at the ideal temperature for up to three hours, with five temp settings between 120 and 145 degrees Fahrenheit. The third-gen version is similar to prior models; however, you can now adjust the heat settings directly on the mug and throw it in the dishwasher, which wasn’t the case before.

Despite being an entry-level variant of the B6 OLED, this model features four HDMI 2.1 ports, a 120Hz refresh rate, a capable processor, and pixel-perfect image quality and contrast for any content you want to watch. Lower brightness is likely the biggest compromise with getting a cheaper OLED.

One of the most affordable Tandem RGB Stripe OLEDs is even cheaper during Black Friday. The AW3226Q monitor has a 165Hz refresh rate, G-Sync compatibility, better-looking text rendering than most other OLED monitors, and unbeatable contrast.

JBL’s Tour One M3 noise-canceling headphones come with a touchscreen-equipped wireless transmitter that lets you wirelessly listen to audio from in-flight entertainment systems and other devices without Bluetooth. They also offer solid active noise cancellation and last up to 70 hours on a charge.

The latest super-rugged wearable from Apple features better battery life than the previous version, plus AI-powered features like Siri Recap also available on the Series 12.

Iniu’s P55-E2 Power Bank is an ultra-slim three-port USB charger that’s capable of fully recharging an iPhone 16 twice. It supports charging speeds of up to 45W via a USB-C port, which can deliver fast recharging for a range of gadgets.

Hisense’s 2026 CanvasTV is a 4K QLED TV that doubles as wall art when you’re not watching. It features a matte, anti-glare display and runs on Google’s excellent TV software; it’s also a great pick for gamers thanks to its snappy 144Hz variable refresh rate and a pair of HDMI 2.1 ports.

The Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 Combo is a beginner-friendly 3D printer that supports four filament spools. It features an enclosed build chamber, automatic bed leveling, and a large touchscreen, making it easy to produce reliable prints.

Moft’s Trackable Tripod Wallet is a MagSafe-compatible wallet that holds two cards and folds into an adjustable phone stand or small tripod. It also supports both Apple’s Find My network and Google’s Find Hub, offers Qi wireless charging, and includes a detachable shutter remote for taking photos.

Birdfy’s metal smart bird feeder features a wide-angle 4K camera that lets you get an up-close look at visiting birds, along with a 1.8-liter seed capacity and a built-in solar panel for charging. It also offers free AI-powered recognition of more than 6,000 bird species.

The Icemag 3 can wirelessly deliver up to 25W of power to compatible smartphones and up to 35W wired charging via USB-C. The 10,000mAh Qi2 charger can also act as a foldable kickstand, comes with an integrated USB-C cable that serves as a lanyard, and sports a transparent design with colorful RGB lighting.

Saros is a third-person sci-fi shooter in which players fight alien enemies on a mysterious planet trapped in a time loop. The PS5 exclusive features fast-paced combat, a variety of powerful weapons, and challenging boss fights. Read our review.

Bose’s second-gen QuietComfort Headphones build on the original with better sound quality and support for lossless audio over USB-C. They also offer improved noise cancellation and are more comfortable thanks to their lack of “eardrum suck.”

The Dreame X60 Ultra is a powerful robot vacuum and mop that does a great job of cleaning carpets thanks to its dual roller brushes and 35,000Pa of suction. It can climb over tall thresholds, squeeze under low furniture, and automatically detach its mop pads when vacuuming carpets.

Garmin’s midrange Forerunner watch has an OLED display, a week’s worth of battery life, and dual-frequency GPS for better accuracy. Read our review.

Samsung’s last-gen Frame is a 4K QLED TV that displays art on its anti-glare matte screen when not in use. It also supports Dolby Atmos, HDR10 Plus, and popular streaming apps, with refresh rates up to 144Hz on larger models.

TP-Link’s Wi-Fi smart plug lets you remotely control lamps, fans, and other appliances using your phone or voice commands. It supports Matter, so it works with all major smart home platforms to set schedules and timers to automatically turn devices on or off.

Google’s latest pair of wireless earbuds features crisp sound, a comfortable design, and solid active noise cancellation, which is great considering the budget-friendly price tag. They even offer built-in support for Gemini and, unlike the entry-level AirPods, a purple option! Read our review.

Roku now makes some of the most affordable, yet feature-packed 4K OLED TVs available for gamers or movie lovers looking for a big TV upgrade under $1,000. The Pro Series LX with better brightness, faster refresh rate, and a polarizer to reduce reflections starts at $200 more.

If you’re on a tight budget, but want spectacular contrast and brightness control that only an OLED can provide, here’s a deal for you. Alienware’s 1440p 27-inch QD-OLED monitor with 240Hz refresh rate is selling at its lowest price yet. Read our hands-on.

The best XPS 13 in years. It doesn’t have a headphone jack and starts with only 8GB of RAM but it’s an excellent thin-and-light with a great screen, a solid Intel chip, and speedy storage.

Soundcore makes some of the best wireless earbuds you’ve never heard of — and the Liberty 5 Pro may be its best pair yet. The sleek buds deliver powerful noise cancellation, good sound, and surprisingly fabulous call quality for less than Apple’s latest AirPods.

The latest Powerbeats Pro are a no-brainer for athletes. They pack fantastic sound and thumping bass, along with active noise cancellation, IPX4 water resistance, and heart rate monitoring. Read our review.

The big difference between the Superstrike and other gaming mice lies beneath its main two mouse buttons. It uses haptic actuators instead of mechanical switches, allowing for lower latency and more longevity.

A great first portable music player/speaker for kids. It uses insertable NFC cards (sold separately) to play music and stories to keep kiddos occupied and entertained without zoning out in front of the TV. This model supports Bluetooth and 3.5mm for private listening, too.

The Nex Playground’s motion-controlled gameplay is designed for ages five and up. It comes with games like Fruit Ninja and Whack-a-Mole Deluxe, but many more titles are available via a subscription. It’s a ton of fun for kids. This is the lowest price so far in 2026. Read our review.

Nothing has changed in terms of aesthetics, but the Max 2 deliver better sound and some new features. Not exactly worth upgrading for, but fantastic for those who are considering them now. Read our full review.

It’s hard to find a cooler lamp than Govee’s Uplighter floor lamp at this price. It can light a room, and display a mesmerizing pattern up your wall and onto your ceiling.

The Meta Quest 3S is a battery-powered standalone VR headset that has the same chipset as the pricier Quest 3, but with the same lenses and screen resolution as the Quest 2. In addition to being able to play many games from the Meta Store, it can also be connected to a gaming PC to play VR games like Half-Life Alyx. Read our review.

Sucker Punch’s follow-up to Ghost of Tsushima is everything you could want in a sequel. The open-world revenge epic brims with fluid combat and a host of welcome narrative twists, all set against the gorgeous backdrop of Japan’s Edo period. It’s precisely the type of game photo modes were made for, even if you never use them.

The Beats 360 are ANC headphones for people who prefer headphones over earbuds at the gym. They’re Beats’ first IP-rated cans, with ear cushions that you can easily remove for cleaning (or style points). They also stay in place during most exercises, while still delivering solid bass. Read our review.

Donkey Kong Bananza is one of the Switch 2’s first exclusive must-have titles. Its destructible environment allows you to smash your way through each of its 17 levels, and the paths you make will remain intact unless you specifically choose to reset the world. Your companion Paulene’s singing allows you to transform into animals that have abilities that allow you to reach previously inaccessible parts of levels. Read our review.

Arguably the best thing to come out of The Book of Boba Fett was the Mandalorian’s N-1 Starfighter, which Lego has recreated here in miniature. It’s not quite as impressive as the 1,802-piece version, but the cheaper set still packs plenty of detail, including a spring-loaded shooter.

Nintendo’s latest Switch 2 exclusive is the best way to relive what is arguably the best Zelda game of all time. The revamped visuals look gorgeous, and while the game’s improved controls might annoy some purists who still cling to the heyday of ’98, we reckon most folks won’t bat an eye.

A 10-inch anti-glare touchscreen that comes in a few design options. It’s a frame that features Alexa, and doubles as a smart speaker. It works with Amazon Photos, which offers unlimited storage for Prime members.

This innovative new smart lock uses the U1 ultra-wideband (UWB) chip in many iPhones and Apple Watches to automatically unlock your door as you approach. It also works with the new Aliro standard, making it compatible with Android phones for hands-free unlocking. Read our review.

Twelve South’s entry-level Bluetooth transmitter delivers up to 25 hours of continuous use and lets you connect up to two pairs of headphones to an in-flight entertainment system, making it a great travel companion no matter where you’re going.

In Catan, up to four players strategically compete and trade for resources. The iconic board game ends when one player reaches 10 “victory points,” which is achieved by constructing a sprawling civilization of roads, settlements, and cities using sheep, ore, wheat, and wood.

Control Resonant is all about manipulation — of gravity, not people. Remedy’s excellent sequel to Control is an exhilarating action game, with ever-changing combat, twisted level design, and the weirdest traversal mechanics we’ve seen in a long time.

Birdbuddy’s charming, camera-equipped feeder identifies and snaps shots of each bird that stops by, supplementing its 5-megapixel stills with insightful facts via an app. The solar roof helps keep the camera’s battery topped up even when it’s cloudy outside.

Azul is a game in which you arrange patterned tiles in order to create the most beautiful tapestry possible. Arranging tiles in a strategic sequence will help you build your score while limiting your opponents’ ability to grow theirs.

Magna-Tiles are a quintessential kids’ toy. The colorful, semi-translucent geometric shapes are a favorite here at The Verge, especially for those of us who prefer the simplicity of building with magnets rather than bricks.

Lego’s 709-piece kit lets you construct three brick-ified bonsai trees, including a black pine, a ginkgo with yellow leaves, and a wisteria with hanging lilac flowers. It also comes with three ornamental displays, just in case you want a raised stand on which to showcase them.

The Beam isn’t as powerful as the Sonos Arc, nor can it match the flagship soundbar’s Dolby Atmos immersion bubble. But you still get room-filling surround sound for less money — and the Beam ties into the Sonos ecosystem for added convenience. Read our review.

Google wants to sell you on the Pro’s software features, but it’s the underlying hardware that makes it a stellar Android handset. The build quality is incredible, the larger telephoto sensor is an improvement, and it now supports faster wired speeds and Qi2.2 for up to 25W wireless charging. Read our review.

Roborock’s first roller-mop robot vacuum, the Curv 2 Flow, features flagship specs at a midrange price, including excellent mopping, a retractable mop cover, 20,000Pa suction, AI-powered obstacle avoidance, and a compact design. Read our review.

The Insta360 Link 2 offers the same auto-swiveling design as its excellent predecessor, only in a smaller form factor. It also offers a slate of new features, including group tracking and no-follow zones.

With 12.4mm drivers, active noise cancellation, and an IP54 rating, the CMF Buds 2A offer high-end features at an affordable price. You can also customize the sound, adjust ANC levels, and find the earbuds using the Nothing X app.

These smart lights have beautiful colors, a nice selection of festive scenes, and an easy-to-use app. They are super reliable when paired with a Hue Bridge and also work over Bluetooth. They come in three lengths, work with all the major smart home platforms, and are Matter-compatible. Read our review.

The Echo Dot Max features a flat design and a redesigned sound system, which delivers nearly three times the bass as its predecessor. It also offers improved conversation detection and better noise filtering, thanks to Amazon’s new AZ3 chip. Read our review.

Glocusent’s clip-in reading light features five brightness levels and multiple color temperature settings, ranging from a soft, warm glow that’s great for late-night reading to a brighter light that’s perfect for daytime use. The slim USB light easily slips into your pocket, too, so you can read anywhere, from a cozy bed to a dimly lit train.

Vantage isn’t your typical open-world exploration game. It’s a sci-fi roguelike that has you traversing an alien planet alongside up to five players, each of whom must solve puzzles and complete their mission before their time, morale, or health runs out. It’s not as charming as Stonemaier’s award-winning Wingspan, but it is far more interesting.

A quiet, battery-powered fan that moves a lot of air despite its small size, the Switchbot Standing Circulator is a surprisingly versatile smart home addition.

The last-gen JBL Go 4 has been around for a bit, but the pocket-sized Bluetooth speaker still delivers with up to seven hours of runtime, dual-device connectivity, and an IP67 rating for water and dust resistance. You can also pair it with other Go 4 speakers for bigger stereo sound, if desired.

Fairphone’s latest is a very light update to the 6, adding a newer processor and carrying forward its repairability and ethical values. Tradeoffs compared to a traditional smartphone are few, and the benefits are real.

The proliferation of miniature screens continues with Ugreen’s latest Nexode USB-C Cable, which features a full-color LCD screen on one end that displays current power draw (up to 240W). It also supports 480Mbps data transfer speeds and, unlike similar power meter-equipped cables, lets you turn off the screen when needed.

The Apple Watch SE 3 is a major glow-up, adding an always-on display, wrist-temperature sensor, a more powerful processor, and fast charging. Read our review.

Nintendo’s latest Pokémon spinoff for the Switch 2 is part Pokémon, part Minecraft, and part Animal Crossing. Yet, despite borrowing gameplay mechanics from each, the cozy life sim is more than the sum of its expansive, building-centric parts. It’s breezy and warm-hearted, with enough secrets to keep mother dearest occupied for hours on end.

Google’s new Pixel 10A introduces faster wired charging, Satellite SOS, and new AI tools like Camera Coach and Auto Best Take. Otherwise, it’s basically the Pixel 9A, with the same Tensor G4 chip and a dual-camera system. Read our review.

The entry-point into RTX Spark laptops, the Asus ProArt is a creator-focused MacBook Pro wannabe with a sleek blacked-out design and lovely OLED display. Read our initial Nvidia RTX Spark hands-on.

There are many gaming headsets out there, but few as elegant as Fractal’s Scape. The PC-focused (but Switch- and PlayStation-compatible) wireless headset offer great sound and include a wireless charger, and they have easy-to-master physical controls.

Everyone knows gift cards aren’t the best gift, but with such steep discounts happening on Nintendo eShop credit, you can save a lot on a Switch 2, or games and accessories, if you’re alright with jumping through a couple extra hoops.

USB-C display glasses can make travel (or relaxing on the couch) more fun by putting a huge virtual screen in front of your face. Xreal’s One Pro are some of the best out there at displaying content from your phone, tablet, laptop, or portable handheld.

Govee’s Permanent Outdoor Lights 2 are Matter-ready smart lights you can leave up year-round. They can display multiple colors at once, with 100 preset lighting scenes, customizable effects, and the ability to sync to music. The lights also feature an IP67 rating for dust and water resistance.

The Ecobee Smart Thermostat Premium is an excellent option for adding smarts and some style to your HVAC system. As well as being a smart way to control your energy use, the thermostat can also act as a video intercom for Ecobee’s excellent doorbell camera and an indoor air quality monitor. Read our review.

Update, November 27th: Updated to include several new picks, including those for Govee’s Permanent Outdoor Lights 2 and the Ecobee Smart Thermostat Premium.
